data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when it is installed under a shown-to-fail-first ritual: the test is authored against a planted mutation that fails before the guard exists, so the test's passing later becomes a certificate of the guard's presence rather than a description of current behavior. The 3-of-26 result is the residue of this installation asymmetry \u2014 mutations lost under shown-to-fail-first installation are exactly those where the test was never re-run against the mutation after the guard landed, while every ordinarily-guarded module at 4/4 to 6/7 shows the same author's ritualized guard-then-test ordering.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3 surviving mutations are all in code paths with no test coverage at all, the loss is a coverage gap rather than an installation-order artifact.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's 1-of-9 loss is attributable to a specific syntactic mutation class that shown-to-fail cannot express, the mechanism is class-specific not ritual-specific.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an ordinarily-guarded module at 6/7 shows the same loss rate as shown-to-fail modules, the installation mode does no differential work.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation-testing harness re-runs all tests against all mutations regardless of installation order, the shown-to-fail ritual cannot cause a loss.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation inverts the evidential direction. In ordinary testing, a mutation is applied to code and the test either catches it or not; the test describes behavior. When the mutation is planted first and the test is shown failing, the subsequent fix installs a guard whose necessity has been pre-established by that failure. The test now constrains the fix \u2014 it passes only because the guard exists \u2014 rather than describing the code. The 1-of-9 loss in compile.py is the failure mode of this ritual: a mutation that would be caught by a test installed under ordinary order is lost when the shown-to-fail sequence terminates early, because the test is never executed against the mutation in the final configuration. The 3-of-26 distribution is the same mechanism at larger scale: mutations that survive are those where the shown-to-fail step was skipped, abbreviated, or the guard was weakened during installation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
